viz_reviews.summary: The page renders the textbook Toulmin diagram, all six slots in labelled regions in the order the framework prescribes. Zero overlapping label pairs, zero off-screen labels, zero labels under cards at the default view in both examples, clean console in every state, examples switch cleanly with no duplicated legend rows or stars. With derived hidden the classic WARRANT box is visibly empty while the 'since' and 'on account of' guides still point into it. The idea-bearing slot is unmissable: gold rings on r2 and r3, a star in each label, a caption inside the REBUTTAL region, a legend row and the idea sentence in the side panel. Both stats lines match graph.json exactly (classic 7/4 nodes, 4/5/7 edges; tbpn 14/6 nodes, 7/12/13 edges); the fact panel shows the verbatim quote plus source_ref and the derived panel confidence, rationale and the supported-by facts. Legibility loses a point only for the arrowhead pile-up on the claim's left face and a few edges crossing rebuttal labels, both cosmetic.

notes:
Research (recall): Stephen Toulmin, The Uses of Argument (1958), a model of practical, field-dependent argument as opposed to the syllogism. Six parts: Claim (what is to be accepted), Grounds/Data (the specific facts appealed to), Warrant (the general, bridge-like inference licence 'if D then C', normally left unstated), Backing (the field-specific assurance behind the warrant: statutes, statistics, expertise), Qualifier (modal strength: presumably, probably, necessarily), Rebuttal (conditions of exception under which the warrant does not license the step). Textbook case: Harry was born in Bermuda, so presumably Harry is a British subject, since a person born in Bermuda is generally a British subject, on account of the relevant statutes, unless both parents were aliens or he has been naturalised elsewhere. Native diagram: grounds at left, arrow to 'so, qualifier, claim' at right, warrant under the arrow ('since'), backing under the warrant ('on account of'), rebuttal hanging off the qualifier ('unless'). Common misuse: warrant restated as a specific claim rather than a general rule; backing confused with grounds (backing supports the warrant, not the claim); rebuttal confused with a counter-claim (it is a condition, not an opposing argument); qualifier dropped so every claim sounds certain. Provenance expectation: grounds and claim are usually stated (fact); warrant is almost always unstated (derived); backing is stated only when the speaker is pressed; qualifier is sometimes stated as a hedge ('probably', 'I think'); rebuttal is occasionally stated ('unless') but mostly derived. No sibling framework is done yet, so house style comes from _meta/sample/graph.json only. Scout: three candidates (Hutchins CLEC-analogy argument 2025-11-19; Levchin BNPL-vs-credit-cards 2025-08-29; Dwarkesh continual-learning 2025-07-07). Chose Hutchins: one speaker, one passage (L4720-4890), all six slots fillable with facts except the warrant, which is genuinely unstated and contestable; a rebuttal is stated by another guest (Byrne Hobart, L3300) in the same file and by the host right after (L4896-4900). Graph: classic = Toulmin Harry/Bermuda case as an original scenario text (warrant unstated so it must be derived); tbpn = 20 nodes (14 fact, 6 derived), 32 edges (7 fact, 25 derived), 0 paraphrases. Validate: 0 errors, 0 warnings. Edge convention: rebuts targets the claim (registry description) rather than the qualifier as in Toulmin's drawing; supported_by links carry each derived node to its facts. idea_bearing_slot = rebuttal: the derived exception conditions name the underserved needs (counterparty-risk rating or insurance for compute offtake; a priced residual-value market for used accelerators).

Viz: 3 iterations, final verdict pass (5 demonstrates / 5 provenance / 4 legibility / 5 fidelity). Iteration 1 passed a critic but sat at the pass rule's maximum, one overlapping label pair in the TBPN default view (b2 'TSMC borrowed Taiwan's rating' against b3 'Old hardware keeps value'), and its suggestions went unapplied. Iteration 2 rebuilt index.html from the template changed in 9184645, split the backing into two rows, made both rebuttal groups columns and added the classic Qualifier region, reaching 0 overlapping pairs; its critic still returned revise at legibility 3, because report.json measures label-label overlap, off-screen and under-card cases but not a label printed across a node marker, which is what was wrong. Iteration 3 found the cause in the shared engine (see engine notes below), patched it page-locally, rebuilt both layouts on the corrected geometry and made the idea-bearing slot visible; its critic passed with no blocking issues. Across all three iterations the builders changed only layout fields, one node size (c1 1.4 to 1.6) and 11 tbpn labels shortened in iteration 1; graph.json with layout fields and labels stripped is identical to the content commits, verified before each viz commit.

Extension block: it is no longer decor only. Besides Toulmin's 'so' beside the arrow row (one position per example) it carries three page-local patches for engine defects, all idempotent and all inside the EXT markers: a ResizeObserver on #stage that re-dispatches the window resize event, an injected '#labels{z-index:1}' rule, and the idea-field treatment (a gold arc-ring on nodes carrying an idea, added as a child of the node object so it hides with the derived toggle, a star in those labels, a caption on the Rebuttal region, a legend row, and the idea sentence at the top of the side panel via a MutationObserver on #panel). Decision: patch locally rather than wait, because _meta is out of a framework agent's reach; when the engine learns these, this block should shrink back to the 'so' decor.

Engine notes for the orchestrator, current as of this commit. The two notes recorded after iteration 1 are fixed and have been removed: the facts-only stats line no longer counts fact edges with a hidden derived endpoint, and the camera fit no longer clips the TBPN Backing row at wide viewports, both fixed in 9184645, which also made derived edges hide with the derived toggle so the facts-only view is source-true. Open, found in iterations 2 and 3 and worth fixing centrally: (1) resize() runs once before the first buildExample() while renderNote() then shortens the stage, so the WebGL drawing buffer keeps the pre-note height and CSS2D labels are placed for the taller viewport; markers are drawn up to about 43px above their own labels at the foot of a tall layout, and the camera mis-fits. Calling resize() at the end of buildExample() fixes it; the note strip's hover-expand re-triggers it. (2) #labels needs z-index: 1, or scene labels paint over the side panel, which is z-index 4. (3) node labels are anchored at (0,-r,0) with no per-node offset, so a label always overlaps the lower half of its own marker and sits inside a cone or diamond silhouette. (4) the engine has no handling for idea or idea_bearing_slot, so every framework will re-implement it in its extension block. (5) safeArea accounts for the side panel only at resetView time, so opening the panel covers whatever is under it. (6) a region caption is centred at (x0+2, y1-2), so half of it hangs outside the region's left edge. (7) the plane fit subtracts sidePad twice, so a plane layout uses about 70% of the available width.

Data judgment left standing, raised by both critics: classic r3 ('Nobody has checked the parents' nationality') has no rebuts edge and so floats in the default and facts-only views. Deliberate: r3 is not a condition under which the claim fails, it is the stated gap that makes exception r1 live, which is exactly what the derived r4 says (ce16, r4 supported_by r3). Adding a rebuts edge to tidy the picture would misread the model, and the link is visible with grounding links on. Same for the six TBPN fact nodes with no fact edge in the facts-only view (c2, b1, b2, b3, r0, r1): under the fact-edge criterion their connections are all inferred, which is the finding, not a defect. Final review fixes (2026-09-10): classic w1 and ce2 lowered from 0.90 to 0.85 (a warrant is the general rule an argument needs, the 0.70-0.85 band). tbpn e4 (g3->c1) and e5 (g4->c1) reclassified fact -> derived 0.80: their quotes were an introductory clause and g4's own text, not a statement of the connection; the rationales now cite the actual closing span ('And so each of the ... contracts and builds right now has a commercial proposition in it', L4866-L4868, 'So it's not, it's not analogous', L4880) and explain that it spans several turns with host interjections.
